triples.name: wealth concentration
triples.description: concentration of money and power that destroys democratic participation (concept paper section 5)

triples.name: market power
triples.description: the ability of a market dominant company to prevent competition, dictate prices and shift profits to low tax jurisdictions (concept paper section 7)

triples.name: biased information
triples.description: incomplete or one sided information used as the basis for political and social decisions (concept paper section 4)

triples.name: artificial intelligence
triples.description: Artificial intelligence is the capability of computational systems to perform tasks typically associated with human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning and decision-making.

triples.name: black-box AI
triples.description: proprietary AI systems without disclosed training data, open source code or accountability chain, which reproduce a text in its intended reading instead of exposing its weaknesses (concept paper section 6)

triples.name: citizen participation
triples.description: the missing overview of the solidarity effects of an initiative, which reduces a multifaceted issue to a binary yes or no decision (concept paper section 10)

triples.name: GDP mismeasurement
triples.description: gross domestic product measures the market production and not the benefit, so free goods count as zero and unrepaired damage does not reduce it (concept paper section 11)

triples.name: proprietary software
triples.description: closed source software in the public sector that causes opacity, missing verifiability, vendor dependency and risks to national security (concept paper section 9)

triples.name: climate gas emissions
triples.description: Greenhouse gas emissions are the release of gases into the atmosphere that trap heat and thereby warm the climate.

triples.name: reduce climate gas emissions
triples.description: a transparent, publicly calculated climate tariff that prices the emissions of imports and exports and thereby stops carbon leakage (concept paper section 3)

triples.name: wrong decisions
triples.description: decisions that do not reach the intended goal, e.g. because the knowledge was incomplete

triples.name: avoid wrong decisions
triples.description: decisions based on precise and neutral knowledge instead of the emotional impulse of the group (concept paper section 4)

triples.name: platform regulation
triples.description: democratically legitimised, transparent and justiciable rules against disinformation on internet platforms (concept paper section 2)

triples.name: Delphi method
triples.description: structured, iterative and anonymised consultation of experts, in a real time variant used to let transparent consensus building set the direction instead of the emotional impulse (concept paper section 4)

triples.name: basic income
triples.description: a proto unconditional basic income implemented as a negative income tax, started so low that almost nobody feels an effect and raised as long as the net effect stays positive (concept paper section 5)

triples.name: public AI
triples.description: AI systems with societal decision relevance organised as a public good with disclosed training data, open source availability and clear liability rules (concept paper section 6)

triples.name: market share
triples.description: Market share is the percentage of the total revenue or sales in a market that a company captures.

triples.name: market share tax
triples.description: supplementary taxation of corporate profits linked to the market share in the smallest relevant market segment and levied where the economic use occurs (concept paper section 7)

triples.name: free software
triples.description: free, secure and transparent software in the public sector following the principle public money, public code (concept paper section 9)

triples.name: fluid democracy
triples.description: a structured, argument based and iterative process in which every citizen can propose, debate and decide binding rules (concept paper section 10)

triples.name: domestic usage
triples.description: the actual usage within one country, the base of the gross domestic usage

triples.name: gross domestic usage
triples.description: a measure of the actual usage instead of the market turnover, so that free goods and avoided damage are part of the result (concept paper section 11)
